notes:
I don't have any notes for you this time, because my research didn't get off the ground. My first attempt sent a dozen searches at once, which went over the tool's usage limit. That used up my remaining tool calls for this turn, so the second attempt was blocked too. As a result I didn't read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the sources actually say, with a URL for every point. So I haven't written any verse notes from memory.

**What I'll do when you ask again:** I'll run the searches and page reads a few at a time so I stay within the limit, in this order:

1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word (Guzik), the Bible Hub and StudyLight commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes) and the Precept Austin page on Ephesians 3.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
   - **v. 3–6, the "mystery":** dispensational vs. covenant readings of the church and Israel (gotquestions.org, bible.org, ligonier.org, thegospelcoalition.org).
   - **v. 19, "filled with all the fullness of God":** Wesley's notes and Wesleyan teaching on entire sanctification (wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com), against Reformed and Lutheran views.
   - **v. 16–17, the Spirit's strengthening and Christ dwelling in the heart:** Pentecostal and charismatic views (pneumareview.com, samstorms.org, ag.org).
3. **Other views:**
   - **Translation and scholarship:** NET Bible notes, especially on v. 15 ("every family" vs. "the whole family") and v. 1 and 14 (Paul breaking off and picking the sentence back up).
   - **Catholic and Orthodox:** Chrysostom's homilies on Ephesians and Aquinas (newadvent.org, ccel.org), plus catholic.com.
   - **Popular modern teaching:** how prosperity or word-of-faith preachers use v. 20 ("immeasurably more"), as the allowed sites describe it.

If you'd like, ask for one part at a time (for example "v. 1–7 first"). That keeps each round smaller and more reliable.
